data.title: Frenchman being deported for causing religious division
data.description: A Frenchman staying on Koh Samui has been ordered to leave Thailand amid accusations his actions stirred religious division and conflict among foreign tourists.

data.title: Video of solitary spectator brings crowd back to struggling zoo in Samut Prakan
data.description: A video of an elephant show going ahead as scheduled in an empty arena with only a single spectator at a crocodile farm and zoo in Samut Prakan province has brought a massive wave of visitors, helping revive the fortunes of the 70-year-old attraction.

data.title: Airport Rail Link delays part of an 'upgrade'
data.description: Trains on the Bangkok-Suvarnabhumi airport service were running every 15 minutes on Monday, instead of the usual nine minutes, drawing complaints from commuters over the lack of a clear explanation for the change..

data.title: Fire damages snack factory in Samut Sakhon
data.description: SAMUT SAKHON - A fire damaged the snack and beverage plant of Srinanaporn Marketing Plc in Krathum Baen district on Monday morning.

data.title: Thai Airways cancels flights to Jakarta, volcanic eruption closes airports
data.description: Thai Airways International cancelled flights to Jakarta on Monday as eight Indonesian airports, including two serving the Indonesian capital, remained closed because of ash from erupting Krakatau volcano.

data.title: Two cuffed after school inspection
data.description: CHON BURI: Two Chinese women were arrested for allegedly working at a school in Bang Lamung district without proper permits.

data.title: WHO praises rubella milestone
data.description: Thailand has been recognised by the World Health Organization (WHO) as having eliminated rubella as a public health issue, marking a significant milestone.

data.title: Rosh Hashanah plan sparks debate
data.description: PHUKET: Residents and businesses on the resort island have raised concerns over a planned Rosh Hashanah event at Chabad House Patong on Sept 11, which is expected to attract up to 2,000 participants.

data.title: Teacher in trouble over beatings
data.description: KALASIN: A teacher faces legal action after allegedly beating pupils with bamboo and a feather duster over unfinished homework.

data.title: Calls grow to regulate influencers as a profession
data.description: <p>Thailand is exploring influencer regulation to protect consumers from harmful content and online scams while preserving creators' freedom of expression.</p>

data.title: Battling the blues - Young at risk from city's fast pace, heavy traffic
data.description: <p>In Bangkok's relentless traffic and fast-paced lifestyle, young people are facing mounting pressures that can lead to depression, self-harm and suicidal behaviour.</p>

data.title: Battling the blues
data.description: <p>In Bangkok's relentless traffic and fast-paced lifestyle, young people are facing mounting pressures that can lead to depression, self-harm and suicidal behaviour.</p>

data.title: Chinese associations 'should reach out to young'
data.description: <p>Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul has urged Thailand's nine Chinese associations to strengthen their role as a bridge with China, attracting younger Chinese investors and technology.</p>

data.title: Farmers oppose EU seed rules in free trade talks
data.description: <p>Farmer, consumer and civil society groups oppose an EU proposal that could tighten companies' rights over seeds, warning it could threaten farmers' rights and food security.</p>

data.title: Budget bill cut ahead of debate
data.description: <p>The 2027 budget bill, worth 3.78 trillion baht, has been cut by 11.162 billion baht ahead of a three-day parliamentary debate on its second and third readings starting on Monday, with MPs set to challenge several major allocations.</p>

data.title: US crew delighted with visit
data.description: <p>The five-day visit of the USS Abraham Lincoln and about 5,000 US Navy personnel ended on Sunday as the aircraft carrier prepared to leave Laem Chabang.</p>

data.title: Oil leak at data centre sparks concerns
data.description: <p>Pollution officials are inspecting a Bangkok data centre after oil-contaminated waste entered drainage pipes, raising concerns that it could reach Rama IX Canal and affect nearby communities.</p>

data.title: Govt set to  appoint new  spokesman
data.description: <p>The government is preparing to reshuffle its communications team, with Ekkapob Pianpises, known as "Dr Ek", tipped to replace Rachada Dhnadirek as government spokesman, according to a source.</p>

data.title: iLaw chief urges public to join rally
data.description: <p>Internet Dialogue on Law Reform (iLaw) director Yingcheep Atchanont has called on the public to join a final rally on Sept 13, a day before the Election Commission (EC) is due to decide whether to prosecute suspects accused of colluding in the 2024 Senate election.</p>

data.title: Foreign interloper gropes woman at cannabis shop
data.description: CHON BURI - Police are hunting a "dark-skinned foreign man" alleged to have sexually molested one woman and kissed another at a cannabis shop in Bang Lamung district in the early hours of Sunday.

data.title: Three students lose millions to fake police, scholarship scam
data.description: Three students lost more than 2.7 million baht to call-centre scams in which the fraudsters posed as police officers and as a university lecturer offering a fake overseas scholarship.

data.title: Accused teen-porn producer made B120,000 a month on OnlyFans
data.description: Police arrested a 32-year-old man accused of luring teenage girls into making pornographic videos, selling the material online and profiting to the tune of 120,000 baht a month.

data.title: Tourists cheat death on winding downhill road
data.description: PHETCHABUN - Four tourists were lucky to survive a downhill car crash on Phu Thap Boek mountain in Lom Kao district on Sunday, saved by a concrete guardrail from plummeting into the valley below

data.title: Ancient rock paintings discovered in Nong Bua Lamphu cave
data.description: NONG BUA LAMPHU - Fine Arts officials have inspected newly found rock paintings believed to be around 4,000 years old in a cave behind a forest monastery in Na Wang district of this northeastern province, in what archaeologists say could be an important addition to Thailand's prehistoric heritage.

data.title: Heavy rain in Northeast, later in Greater Bangkok and other regions
data.description: Heavy rain is forecast in the Northeast early this week and then in Greater Bangkok and other regions until Friday.
